source.publication: 2025 DR 0104 Booklet (Colorado Individual Income Tax), DR 0104 and DR 0104AD
source.section: DR 0104AD line 3 / line 5 Social Security Benefits (PDF p.18 Line 3; p.19 Line 5; DR 0104AD p.1 lines 3 and 5), 55-64 single federal AGI not over 75,000; DR 0104 lines 1, 10-13 (PDF p.8, p.10); tax table PDF p.34-35

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 45,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 70,500.00. Taxable Social Security on gross benefits 30,000.00 (you): federal SS worksheet (given): half of benefits 15,000.00 + other income 45,000.00 = 60,000.00; less 25,000.00 = 35,000.00; line 11 = 26,000.00; line 13 = half of smaller of 35,000.00 and 9,000.00 = 4,500.00; line 14 = 4,500.00; line 15 = 85% x 26,000.00 = 22,100.00; line 16 = 26,600.00; 85% of benefits = 25,500.00; taxable Social Security = 25,500.00. Federal taxable income = 70,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 54,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). DR 0104 line 1 federal taxable income (Form 1040 line 15) 54,750.00; lines 2-9 additions 0.00 (no state income tax addback, no other-state bond interest; federal AGI 70,500.00 is not over 300,000, so no line 4 deduction addback); line 10 subtotal 54,750.00. DR 0104AD: Line 3 (primary taxpayer, age 63, 55-64): federal AGI (DR 0104 line 34) 70,500.00 does not exceed 75,000.00 (single), so the entire taxable Social Security 25,500.00 (better than the 20,000-limited subtraction, smaller of 25,500.00 and 20,000.00 = 20,000.00). Line 22 subtotal = 25,500.00; DR 0104 line 11 = 25,500.00. Line 12 Colorado taxable income = 54,750.00 - 25,500.00 = 29,250.00. Line 13 tax = 4.4% x 29,250.00 = 1,287.00 (the tax table row over 29,200.00 but not over 29,300.00, PDF p.35, gives 1,287.00; expected keeps the formula figure). No credits claimed: 0.00. Colorado income tax 1,287.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax is figured on the exact income at 4.4%; below 50,000 the booklet uses the tax table, which taxes each 100-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds to the dollar.
